title: [Native DSL] Split overrides into (cond, impl) callables
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.14.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #181385

Summary:

Rework the override API so callers register a predicate and an
implementation separately instead of a single fused callable with a
fallback-kernel kwarg. The registry now also materializes each
override as an opaque `_native::<id>` op with a schema cloned from
the aten op it overrides, letting the eager router dispatch to it by
name.

Eager routing captures the prior aten kernel via
`torch.library.get_kernel(...)` before installing the override and
falls back through it (via `call_boxed`) when no cond matches, which
keeps autograd's backward formulas recursion-safe. The aten
override is held in a per-(op, dispatch_key) `torch.library.Library`
so it can be cleanly destroyed on deregister / reenable.

This is partially a good change to be made early in native-DSL's
lifetime to make the API easier to use on the backend, and partially
a precursor to some tracing/export work to come.

This allows a single (auto-generated) routing operator to be registered to 
dispatch, which then redispatches to each actual override. This pattern
is a little cleaner, with one override registered per "chain" of ops, and 
potentially more performant, with only one C++ -> python jump necessary
during dispatch. The same form of routing op can also be plugged into
tracing via. a meta registration, and the easy-to-access implementations
will be easier to pass down to AOTInductor and beyond.

Test Plan:

```
pytest -sv test/python_native
```

Signed-off-by: Simon Layton <simonlayton@meta.com>
